question: How many world records will be set at the 2026 World Aquatics Swimming Championships?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: recent short-course worlds produced 4 (2021), 14 (2022) and ~30 (2024, per World Aquatics) world records. 2026 form is very strong: 6 WRs at US SC Trials (Oct 28-31, 2026) plus several World Cup WRs (Kornev, Matsushita, Coetze). Marchand debuts, Russians fully readmitted (Kolesnikov, Kornev, Chikunova), McIntosh/Walsh/Douglass/Kos expected, and it is not a post-Olympic hangover year. Against: many records were just lowered in 2024-26 so targets are tougher, and trial-peaking may sap form; 2024's 30 was exceptional. Market check: the only related contracts were harness-supplied Polymarket per-event WR markets, all at 0.50; none prices the total count, and my own search found no total-count market. Median ~15, right tail to >30 priced at ~7%.
calls.dossier:
- Event: World Aquatics Swimming Championships (25m), Beijing, Dec 1-6, 2026 (RIA Novosti 2026-11-13; Swimming World). Resolves off OmegaTiming results / credible sources counting new WRs set at the meet.
- Event window: Dec 1 -> Dec 6, 2026 per meet schedule; as of 2026-11-13 0% elapsed.
- Past SC Worlds WR counts: 2021 Abu Dhabi = 4 (SwimSwam); 2022 Melbourne = 14 (SwimSwam; some sources say 15); 2024 Budapest = 30 per World Aquatics article (Wikipedia US-team summary attributes 21 to the US; ties and relays included). Older editions (2012-2018) roughly single digits to ~10 (background, not verified this run).
- 2026 US SC Trials (Oct 28-31, 2026, Westmont IL): 6 WRs: Douglass 50 free 22.75 (tie) and 100 free 49.64; Berkoff 50 back 25.21; Curzan 100 back 53.92; Mathias 100 breast 55.14; Alexy 100 free 44.84 (tie) (World Aquatics news). US roster 38 athletes.
- 2026 World Cup (Oct): Kornev tied 100 free 44.84 and set 50 back 21.28; Matsushita 400 IM 3:54.33; Coetze 50 back 22.09 (NBC; search summaries). Swimming World (Oct 13, 2026): 4 SCM WRs in 2026 so far at that date, 13 LCM.
- Kos set SCM 100/200 back WRs in fall 2025 (100 back 48.16).
- Expected attendees: Marchand (first SC Worlds), McIntosh, Walsh, Douglass, Smith, Kos, Alexy, Dressel (Swimming World). Russia fully readmitted Apr 13, 2026; 43-swimmer team incl. Kolesnikov, Kornev, Chikunova (RIA, 2026-11-13).
- Against more records: many SCM records were freshly lowered in 2024-26, and athletes peaked for trials/World Cup weeks earlier. 2024's count followed an unusual post-Olympic Walsh/Smith/Douglass surge.
- Mixed relays and ties count as WRs in typical tallies; a record broken twice at the meet (e.g., semis then final) may count twice depending on the source.
- Searched for but not found: a human betting market on the total WR count (only Polymarket per-event WR markets exist); full verified per-edition counts for 2012-2018.

Upside: Marchand's SC Worlds debut (400/200 IM targets), Walsh in WR form (22.75 50 free Oct 2026), Dressel return, deep US team, Russians (Kornev 100 free WR 44.84) readmitted, relays prone to WRs. Market check: the Polymarket per-event WR markets are listed at 0.50, which looks like placeholder pricing; there is no market on the total count, so none was used as an anchor. Median ~12.

calls.reconciliation: McIntosh attendance was disputed: Runs 2 and 3 cite roster reports excluding her, Run 1 only a preview listing her; I accepted her absence. The Alexy 44.84 vs 44.64 discrepancy is unresolved but immaterial. The pre-2021 counts are unverified, so the reference class carries extra uncertainty. Weighing 2024 as a partial outlier against strong 2026 form is a judgment call; I land at median 13, below Runs 1 and 3 because McIntosh is absent, and above Run 2 because of the dense record-setting in October 2026. Carried forward a dispersion of ~18, close to Runs 1 and 3.
